intent: One resizable region of a ResizablePanelGroup, holding any content and sized by the group's handles within its own limits.
typical_uses: One pane of a split view, such as a list, an editor or a preview

dont_use_when.situation: A bordered, padded box that groups a section of content

invariants.text: `defaultSize`, `minSize`, `maxSize` and `collapsedSize` read a number as pixels and a string with no unit as a percentage of the group; a string may also carry `px`, `%`, `em`, `rem`, `vh` or `vw`.

The panel renders two divs: the outer one carries `id`, `data-panel` and every other forwarded attribute, and `className` and `style` go to the inner div that holds the children. The kit applies no class to either.
A `collapsible` panel dragged below the midpoint between its `collapsedSize` (0% when unset) and its `minSize` collapses to `collapsedSize`; between that midpoint and `minSize` it stays at `minSize`.

anti_patterns.dont: Expect the panel to draw a border, a background or padding of its own
anti_patterns.do_instead: Style the content placed inside it, or pass `className`, which lands on the inner element

defaultSize.states: defaultSize is the panel's starting size, a number of pixels or a string size
defaultSize.because: `number | string`, read as `size-units` describes, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property. Without it the panel takes an even share of the group.

minSize.states: minSize is the smallest size a drag can give the panel, a number of pixels or a string size
minSize.because: `number | string`, read as `size-units` describes, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It defaults to 0%.

maxSize.states: maxSize is the largest size a drag can give the panel, a number of pixels or a string size
maxSize.because: `number | string`, read as `size-units` describes, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It defaults to 100%.

collapsedSize.states: collapsedSize is the size a collapsible panel snaps to, a number of pixels or a string size
collapsedSize.because: `number | string`, read as `size-units` describes, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It defaults to 0% and has an effect only with `collapsible`.

elementRef.states: elementRef is a ref to the panel's outer div element
elementRef.because: `Ref<HTMLDivElement | null>` is a union of a ref object and a callback function - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

panelRef.states: panelRef receives the panel's imperative handle, with collapse, expand, getSize, isCollapsed and resize
panelRef.because: `Ref<PanelImperativeHandle | null>` is a ref object or a callback holding an object of functions, which no JSON Schema type covers.

onResize.states: onResize is a callback called with the panel's new size, its id and its previous size, not a value
onResize.because: `(panelSize, id, prevPanelSize) => void`, where a size carries `asPercentage` and `inPixels` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

style.states: style is a plain style object applied inline to the panel's inner div
style.because: `CSSProperties` is React's style object type, which the compiler leaves to tsc; it lands on the inner element that holds the children, not on the panel element.

unexposed_parts.reason: The wrapped Panel renders an inner div inside the panel element that holds the children and receives `className` and `style`; it is not a component of its own.

good.title: A collapsible side panel with size limits in percent
good.code:
<ResizablePanel id="nav" defaultSize="25%" minSize="15%" maxSize="40%" collapsible>
  Navigation
</ResizablePanel>

bad.title: A number meant as a percentage
bad.why: Numbers are pixels, so this panel starts at 30px wide with a 20px minimum; write `"30%"` and `"20%"` for a share of the group.
